name: Plumbing & Water Systems

objectives.text: Identify common plumbing fittings, valves, and pipe materials used on a farm
Identify basic plumbing hand tools such as pipe cutters, pipe wrenches, and deburring tools and state the safe use of each
Describe the path water takes from a farm well or main line to a point of use such as a hydrant or stock tank
Explain how gravity, elevation, and pipe size affect water pressure and flow in a farm water line
Measure pipe and select fittings by nominal size, material, and connection type for a simple plumbing job
Demonstrate proper technique for cutting, joining, and pressure-testing a section of pipe
Explain how a pressure tank and pump pressure switch maintain consistent water pressure in a farm system
Explain how backflow preventers and check valves protect drinking water for people and livestock from contamination
Explain how frost depth, frost-free hydrants, and line drainage protect farm water lines from freezing
Install a drip irrigation line with a filter, pressure regulator, and emitters for a garden or greenhouse project
Compare copper, PVC, PEX, polyethylene, and galvanized steel pipe for cost, durability, pressure rating, and suitability to farm uses
Select and safely use the correct tools and equipment for a plumbing task in an agricultural structure
Install or repair a plumbing fixture such as a frost-free hydrant, automatic livestock waterer, or wash station in an agricultural facility
Explain how drain slope, traps, and venting allow wash-down and waste water to drain properly from barns and processing areas
Analyze how interactions between groundwater and surface water affect the yield and reliability of farm wells, springs, and ponds
Calculate daily water demand and required flow rate in gallons per minute for a livestock operation or irrigated planting
Interpret a farm well water test and recommend treatment options for problems such as bacteria, nitrates, hardness, or iron
Diagnose a farm water system problem such as low pressure, short cycling, or a leak and recommend the repair
Construct the pump, supply, and return plumbing for a recirculating hydroponic or aquaponic system
Design a watering system layout for a livestock facility that sizes pipe, selects materials, and specifies fixtures for expected demand

changes: Kept all six existing objectives, rewording a few for precision and expanding the diagnosis objective to include recommending a repair. Added missing competencies across the span: plumbing tool identification and use, pressure and flow principles, measuring and selecting fittings, backflow prevention, freeze protection, drip irrigation installation, comparing pipe materials, installing fixtures, drain, waste, and vent basics, groundwater effects on well and pond supply, water demand calculation, well water test interpretation, and hydroponic or aquaponic plumbing. Standards are attached only at grades 9 to 11 where an objective directly teaches them. Hydraulic machinery and soil water standards were left unused because they belong to other strands, and wiring, building construction, and site layout are left to the sibling sub-topics.
